rationale: Round 1 built and ran cleanly, so this candidate shifts weight toward stronger obfuscation while protecting ary3's dominant characteristic: a tight, heavily iterated numeric kernel in a 512-byte, 2-function image where any per-iteration overhead is amplified enormously. SUB is cheap and correct, so it gets the highest security/diversity weights as the always-on baseline; SPLIT is nearly free and increases basic-block fragmentation, which amplifies the effect of FLA/IBR on the few large functions present. IBR and IGV add strong control-flow and inter-block ambiguity at low runtime cost, so they are favored next. FLA and BCF are deliberately moderated (BCF especially, since bogus-loop injection lands directly in the hot multiply-accumulate loop of ary3), and ICALL is kept moderate because indirect-call lowering adds dispatch cost inside inner loops and slightly higher correctness risk. All cost and risk weights stay low across the board to keep the tiny binary's size growth and the benchmark's runtime within acceptable bounds while still meaningfully raising reverse-engineering resistance over round 1.
